source_refs.note: Exercise 8.3, Question 4: book page 162 (PDF 167); no answer in key (PDF 307). Misprints: (i) denominator should be sqrt(1+x); (iii) 17/284 should be 17/384.

blocks.prompt: 4 (i) If \(x\) is so small that its square and higher powers can be neglected, then show that \(\frac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 - x}} \approx 1 - \frac{3}{2}x\)
blocks.explanation:
An approximation with \(x^{2}\) neglected: keep only \(1 + nx\) of every series.
But first look at the printed left side: \(\frac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 - x}}\) simplifies exactly to \(\sqrt{1 - x}\).
Plan: expand the printed expression honestly, then show the stated result for the intended expression \(\frac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 + x}}\) (see the correction below).
steps:
Given: \(\frac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 - x}}\), \(x^{2}\) and higher powers negligible.
To show (as printed): \(\approx 1 - \frac{3}{2}x\).
Method: Since \(x^{2}, x^{3}, \dots\) are neglected, each bracket is expanded only as far as \(1 + nx\), and any product of two \(x\)-terms is dropped.

Simplify the printed left side
\[\dfrac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 - x}} = (1 - x)^{1 - \frac{1}{2}}\]
\[= (1 - x)^{1/2}\]
Why: \(\tfrac{a}{a^{1/2}} = a^{1/2}\).

Expand to the \(x\) term
\[(1 - x)^{1/2} \approx 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}(-x)\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x\]
Why: \(1 + nx\) with \(n = \tfrac{1}{2}\) and \(-x\) in place of \(x\).

Compare with the printed result
\[1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x \ne 1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x\]
Why: So the printed statement cannot be shown; the denominator is a misprint. With \(\sqrt{1 + x}\) in the denominator it works:

Intended expression as a product
\[\dfrac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 + x}} = (1 - x)(1 + x)^{-1/2}\]
Why: \(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{a}} = a^{-1/2}\).

Multiply and neglect \(x^{2}\)
\[(1 - x)\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x\right)\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x - x + \dfrac{1}{2}x^{2}\]
\[\approx 1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x\]
Why: The \(\tfrac{1}{2}x^{2}\) term is neglected; \(-\tfrac{1}{2}x - x = -\tfrac{3}{2}x\).

Check
\[x = 0.01:\ \dfrac{0.99}{\sqrt{1.01}} = 0.985087\]
\[1 - 0.015 = 0.985\]
Why: Agrees to the size of the neglected \(x^{2}\) term (about 0.0001).
blocks.final_answer: As printed: \(\frac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 - x}} = \sqrt{1 - x} \approx 1 - \frac{1}{2}x\). The stated result holds for \(\frac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 + x}} \approx 1 - \frac{3}{2}x\). Hence proved (with the corrected denominator).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the left side as \(\frac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 - x}}\). That expression equals \(\sqrt{1 - x} \approx 1 - \frac{1}{2}x\), so it cannot be \(\approx 1 - \frac{3}{2}x\). The printed result is correct for \(\frac{1 - x}{\sqrt{1 + x}}\), which is what we proved.

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) If \(x\) is so small that its square and higher powers can be neglected, then show that \(\frac{\sqrt{1 + 2x}}{\sqrt{1 - x}} \approx 1 + \frac{3}{2}x\)
blocks.explanation:
An approximation with \(x^{2}\) neglected.
Write the left side as \((1 + 2x)^{1/2}(1 - x)^{-1/2}\) and keep only \(1 + nx\) of each.
Plan: expand both, multiply, drop the \(x^{2}\) term, compare.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{\sqrt{1 + 2x}}{\sqrt{1 - x}}\), \(x^{2}\) and higher powers negligible.
To show: \(\approx 1 + \frac{3}{2}x\).
Method: Since \(x^{2}, x^{3}, \dots\) are neglected, each bracket is expanded only as far as \(1 + nx\), and any product of two \(x\)-terms is dropped.

Write as a product
\[\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + 2x}}{\sqrt{1 - x}} = (1 + 2x)^{1/2}(1 - x)^{-1/2}\]
Why: Roots are powers \(\tfrac{1}{2}\); the denominator moves up with power \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\).

Expand each bracket
\[(1 + 2x)^{1/2} \approx 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}(2x) = 1 + x\]
\[(1 - x)^{-1/2} \approx 1 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(-x)\]
\[= 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}x\]
Why: \(1 + nx\) with the whole second term (\(2x\) or \(-x\)) in place of \(x\).

Multiply and neglect \(x^{2}\)
\[(1 + x)\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2}x\right)\]
\[= 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}x + x + \dfrac{1}{2}x^{2}\]
\[\approx 1 + \dfrac{3}{2}x\]
Why: Drop \(\tfrac{1}{2}x^{2}\); \(x + \tfrac{1}{2}x = \tfrac{3}{2}x\).

Check
\[x = 0.01:\ \sqrt{\dfrac{1.02}{0.99}} = 1.015038\]
\[1 + 0.015 = 1.015\]
Why: The difference is of the size of \(x^{2}\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) If \(x\) is so small that its square and higher powers can be neglected, then show that \(\frac{(9 + 7x)^{1/2} - (16 + 3x)^{1/4}}{4 + 5x} \approx \frac{1}{4} - \frac{17}{284}x\)
blocks.explanation:
Three brackets, none starting with 1: take out \(9\), \(16\) and \(4\) first.
Keep only \(1 + nx\) of each series, then multiply the numerator by \((4 + 5x)^{-1}\).
Plan: numerator, denominator, product, compare (the printed 284 is a misprint for 384; see the correction).
steps:
Given: \(\frac{(9 + 7x)^{1/2} - (16 + 3x)^{1/4}}{4 + 5x}\), \(x^{2}\) and higher powers negligible.
To show: \(\approx \frac{1}{4} - \frac{17}{284}x\) (as printed).
Method: Make every bracket start with 1 by taking a number outside; then since \(x^{2}, x^{3}, \dots\) are neglected, each bracket is expanded only as far as \(1 + nx\), and any product of two \(x\)-terms is dropped.

First bracket
\[(9 + 7x)^{1/2} = 3\left(1 + \dfrac{7x}{9}\right)^{1/2}\]
\[\approx 3\left(1 + \dfrac{7x}{18}\right) = 3 + \dfrac{7}{6}x\]
Why: \(9^{1/2} = 3\); \(\tfrac{1}{2} \cdot \tfrac{7x}{9} = \tfrac{7x}{18}\); \(3 \cdot \tfrac{7}{18} = \tfrac{7}{6}\).

Second bracket
\[(16 + 3x)^{1/4} = 2\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{16}\right)^{1/4}\]
\[\approx 2\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{64}\right) = 2 + \dfrac{3}{32}x\]
Why: \(16^{1/4} = 2\); \(\tfrac{1}{4} \cdot \tfrac{3x}{16} = \tfrac{3x}{64}\).

Numerator
\[\left(3 + \dfrac{7}{6}x\right) - \left(2 + \dfrac{3}{32}x\right)\]
\[= 1 + \left(\dfrac{112}{96} - \dfrac{9}{96}\right)x\]
\[= 1 + \dfrac{103}{96}x\]
Why: LCM of 6 and 32 is 96.

Denominator
\[(4 + 5x)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(1 + \dfrac{5x}{4}\right)^{-1}\]
\[\approx \dfrac{1}{4}\left(1 - \dfrac{5}{4}x\right)\]
Why: \(4^{-1} = \tfrac{1}{4}\); \(1 + nx\) with \(n = -1\).

Multiply and neglect \(x^{2}\)
\[\dfrac{1}{4}\left(1 + \dfrac{103}{96}x\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{120}{96}x\right)\]
\[\approx \dfrac{1}{4}\left(1 - \dfrac{17}{96}x\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{17}{384}x\]
Why: \(\tfrac{5}{4} = \tfrac{120}{96}\); \(103 - 120 = -17\); \(4 \times 96 = 384\).

Check
\[x = 0.01:\ \text{L.H.S.} = 0.2495573\]
\[\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{17}{384}(0.01) = 0.2495573\]
Why: Agrees to seven decimals; with 284 the value would be 0.2494014, clearly worse.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the right side as \(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{17}{284}x\). The correct result is \(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{17}{384}x\), since \(\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{17}{96} = \frac{17}{384}\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (iv) If \(x\) is so small that its square and higher powers can be neglected, then show that \(\frac{\sqrt{4 + x}}{(1 - x)^{3}} \approx 2 + \frac{25}{4}x\)
blocks.explanation:
An approximation with \(x^{2}\) neglected: \((4 + x)^{1/2}(1 - x)^{-3}\).
Take 4 outside the first bracket, keep \(1 + nx\) of each.
Plan: expand both, multiply, drop \(x^{2}\), compare.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{\sqrt{4 + x}}{(1 - x)^{3}}\), \(x^{2}\) and higher powers negligible.
To show: \(\approx 2 + \frac{25}{4}x\).
Method: Since \(x^{2}, x^{3}, \dots\) are neglected, each bracket is expanded only as far as \(1 + nx\), and any product of two \(x\)-terms is dropped.

Write as a product
\[\dfrac{\sqrt{4 + x}}{(1 - x)^{3}} = (4 + x)^{1/2}(1 - x)^{-3}\]
Why: Root = power \(\tfrac{1}{2}\); denominator up with power \(-3\).

Expand each bracket
\[(4 + x)^{1/2} = 2\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{4}\right)^{1/2} \approx 2\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{8}\right)\]
\[(1 - x)^{-3} \approx 1 + (-3)(-x) = 1 + 3x\]
Why: \(4^{1/2} = 2\); \(\tfrac{1}{2} \cdot \tfrac{x}{4} = \tfrac{x}{8}\); for the second, \(n = -3\) and \(-x\) in place of \(x\).

Multiply and neglect \(x^{2}\)
\[2\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{8}\right)(1 + 3x)\]
\[\approx 2\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{8} + 3x\right)\]
\[= 2\left(1 + \dfrac{25}{8}x\right) = 2 + \dfrac{25}{4}x\]
Why: \(\tfrac{1}{8} + 3 = \tfrac{25}{8}\); then \(2 \cdot \tfrac{25}{8} = \tfrac{25}{4}\).

Check
\[x = 0.01:\ \dfrac{\sqrt{4.01}}{0.99^{3}} = 2.063795\]
\[2 + 0.0625 = 2.0625\]
Why: The difference (about 0.0013) is of the size of the neglected \(x^{2}\) terms, whose coefficient here is about 12.7.
